title: Fixed-free-domain form control forces at least quadratic cutoff decay of the quartic coupling

running_coupling_boundary.scaled_interaction: Use g_N V_N plus arbitrary deterministic vacuum and quadratic counterterms on the unchanged free form domain
running_coupling_boundary.necessary_bound: K1439 gives ||(H_0+1)^(-1/2) g_N W_N||^2>=c |g_N|^2 N^4, so any cutoff-uniform form bound requires |g_N|=O(N^-2)
running_coupling_boundary.fixed_coupling_consequence: Every fixed nonzero coupling, and every running coupling with N^2|g_N| unbounded, fails this necessary free-form-domain test
running_coupling_boundary.conditional_escape: A coupling with |g_N|=O(N^-2) only removes this one vacuum-sector obstruction; it does not prove a nonzero interacting limit, semiboundedness, closability, convergence on other particle sectors, or source ownership
running_coupling_boundary.renormalization_ceiling: The result says nothing against domain dressing, wavefunction or quartic-sector counterterms, non-Gaussian reference measures, or a strong-resolvent limit not obtained by fixed-domain KLMN convergence
